g.text: Caching Strategies — where each pattern touches cache vs. DB, and in what order
Same read/write, four different patterns for who talks to what
2. miss → query DB, app writes result back
App owns both hops — talks to cache AND
db directly. A missed invalidation path
serves stale data forever, not just for a TTL.
2. synchronous write, waits for DB ack
Write latency = cache write + DB write,
every single time. In exchange, a read
right after a write is always fresh.
Fastest writes — but a cache node dying
before flush loses data. Needs a durable
queue in front of the flush to be safe.
2. cache itself fetches on miss — app
Transparent to the app: same call whether
it's a hit or a miss underneath. Miss-fetch
logic lives in the cache layer, not the app.
